gaps.sentence: Nobody explained the reason ___ the flight was cancelled.
gaps.explanation: 'Why' introduces the cause after 'the reason'; it means 'for which'.

gaps.sentence: Pablo, ___ speaks five languages, works as an interpreter.
gaps.explanation: Non-defining clauses about people take 'who'; 'that' never follows a comma in standard English.

gaps.sentence: The discussion got to a stage ___ nobody was listening any more.
gaps.explanation: 'A stage where ...' means 'a stage at which ...'; the clause has its own subject and verb, so 'which' is impossible.

gaps.sentence: We arrived at the hotel at noon, ___ the rooms were not ready.
gaps.explanation: 'When' introduces non-defining clauses about time after a comma; 'that' is impossible after a comma.

gaps.sentence: The village, ___ population has halved since the mine closed, is seeking city funding.
gaps.explanation: The population belongs to the village: whose population.

gaps.sentence: The man ___ lives next door is a doctor.
gaps.explanation: 'Who' refers to people as the subject of the clause; 'which' is for things and 'whose' shows possession.

gaps.sentence: My laptop, ___ I bought only last year, has already crashed twice.
gaps.explanation: Non-defining clause about a thing: 'which', never 'that'.

gaps.sentence: The reason ___ the flight was diverted has never been made public.
gaps.explanation: 'The reason why' — 'why' is the relative for reasons.
